title: Stored, Not Integrated: A Pre-Treatment Predictor and Three Controls for Knowledge Injection
description:
Fine-tuning stores new facts almost perfectly and leaves them unusable: injected-fact recall is 1.000 while two-hop composition using the same fact is 0.22. This record contains the code, constructed datasets and results behind a measurement of what determines whether an injected fact becomes usable, and whether that can be predicted before injection.

Composition scales with a per-item measurement taken on the base model before injection (Spearman rho = +0.225, n = 1554, three seeds; positive within five of six templates), and the dependence is relational rather than entity familiarity. Training the model to generate the bridge entity (0.000 to 1.000) yields no gain over a control that trains an unrelated fact. Supplying the bridge in context raises composition from 0.220 to 0.498, but a false-bridge control shows approximately 73 percent of that gain does not depend on the bridge being correct. A commit/defer gate on the predictor raises composition among committed facts from 0.144 to 0.207, with a threshold that transfers across seeds. Two experiments returned negative results. A published self-patching recovery figure is measured against a baseline of zero where the appropriate null per-item maximum is +0.80.
